current.text: He joined Milwaukee from Miami in the Giannis Antetokounmpo trade.
He is projected to start at forward. The projected opening lineup is Rollins, Herro, Jaquez, Kuzma and Turner. Milwaukee's power forward group is very thin.
The starting lineup could change by December or March, so his starting role is not secure.
A trade is possible. The experts say the roster needs trades to consolidate and that he does not fit well with Kuzma, Porter and Herro. One note named Denver as a possible destination.
His assists should drop because Milwaukee has so many ball handlers.
Much of his production last season came when two or three Miami players were out, Herro among them. Herro is now his teammate in Milwaukee.
The expert does not trust his late-season shooting surge and sees little upside. He is fine only as a late flyer.
Milwaukee is expected to be a bad team. Its win total is 26.5. New coach Taylor Jenkins might use a deep rotation.

durable.text: The experts see him as a low-end player: at best a sixth man, or a seventh or eighth man on a good team. He needs opportunity and usage to produce.
One expert calls him a bad shooter.
He makes few threes for a guard or forward.
He gets few steals and blocks.

note: He sits at the edge of our 144-player pool. Yahoo ranks him 135, ESPN 148, and both price him at about 1 USD, so spend no more than 1 USD as a late flyer, mainly in punt 3PM builds. The two sites' projections differ a lot (54.2 vs 50.2 FG%, 1.0 vs 1.9 TO), and his value depends on the FG% and assists, since the expert expects the assists to fall among Milwaukee's many guards. Early in the season, check whether he holds the starting forward spot, whether his assists stay near 4 to 5 next to Herro and Rollins, and whether a trade happens.
